findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM THE 12/11/2023 INSPECTION. 

Observed a previously wet wiping cloth stored in an empty bucket. Wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer between uses and once soiled immediately separated for laundering. Wet cloths are not allowed to sit in empty buckets or other surfaces within the facility when not in use. Ensure that wiping cloths are stored properly by the next routine inspection. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Facility has several repeat and priority/priority foundation violations. Violations are severe enough to require the facility to be ordered to cease use of the soda fountain. Additionally, active managerial control appears to be lacking as several violations appeared to be regular occurrences which person-in-charge blamed on staff. Ultimately, person-in-charge is responsible for ensuring that the facility remains in compliance with ALL 2017 FDA Food Code requirements as adopted and establishing appropriate corrective actions for failure to comply with these requirements. Inspector did not observe any corrective actions occurring within the establishment. Inspector will return on 1/11/2023 to ensure compliance with ALL priority/priority foundation violations and active managerial control at that time. 

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
THIS IS AREPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION DATED 09/13/2022.

Inspector did not observe any hand washing occurring within the facility and hand sink was fully blocked during the inspection. Employees must wash hands when handling food and any time contamination of the hands may occur. Hands must be washed between cleaning/stocking/handling food to ensure that cross contamination. Inspector observed foods grabbed from the walk-in cooler without hand washing prior to handling the food/packages of food. A follow-up is issued for Thursday 12/14/2023 to ensure compliance with hand washing requirements.

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION DATED 9/13/2022.

Hand washing sinks are required to be accessible for employee hand washing at all times. The hand sink in the back was completely blocked with cleaner, cups and other items. Ensure that hand sinks are unblocked, used only for hand washing, and fully stocked at all times of operations. A follow-up is issued for 12/21/2023 to ensure compliance with hand sink requirements.

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food received at proper temperature
findings.comment:
Inspector checked temperatures of foods delivered from prairie farms and dropped in front of the beer cooler before being brought into the walk-in cooler. Temperatures were between 42 and 50 degrees on arrival. These foods were immediately moved to the walk-in cooler after checking temperatures. However, operator did not check the condition of foods on arrival. A process must be in place to ensure that foods received by the facility are stored at the proper temperatures and are received at the proper temperatures including not being allowed to sit before being placed in coolers. Discussed with operator about establishing a plan for receiving foods. A follow-up is issued for 12/14/2023 to check compliance with receiving requirements. 

3-202.11: (A) TCS FOOD shall be at 41F or below when received-P. (B) If specified by LAW, FOOD may be received at different temperature-P. (C) Eggs shall be received at 45F-P. (D) TCS FOODS already cooked shall be received at 135F or above-P. (E) Frozen FOOD shall be received frozen (Pf). (F) TCS FOOD shall be free of evidence of temperature abuse -Pf.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM INSPECTION DATED 09/13/2022. 

The soda nozzles and ice dispensers of the soda fountain are soiled with mold. Mold growth on the soda nozzles were confirmed with a white paper towel used to wipe the inside of the nozzles. Clear beverages were visibly soiled with dark material. Green and/or brown mold growth was observed in each ice dispenser. Additionally, the drain for the soda fountain is nearly completely blocked with a mass of mold with several different colors including black, white and red. Due to the extent of the mold growth, both soda fountains have been closed for service. The facility is NOT PERMITTED to operate the soda fountain until the ice machine/soda fountains have been completely cleaned and sanitized. Once cleaned, contact SCDPH inspector to schedule a return visit. If no contact is made with SCDPH prior to 12/14/2023, inspector will return on this date to determine the status of the machines.

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
A toxic cleaner spray bottle was observed stored in the cupboard underneath the counter next to mustard and single-use items. Toxic chemicals must be stored in a manner that prevents the possibility of contamination of foods and food-contact surfaces including single-service/single-use items. A follow-up is issued for 12/14/2023 to ensure compliance with toxic chemical storage requirements. 

7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Inspector observed x4 cockroaches on-or-near the electrical box near the drain for the soda fountain. These roaches were large adults and highly active with no indication of poisoning from pesticide use. A single young cockroach was observed between the two counters near the soda fountain. In total, x5 cockroaches were observed during the inspection today. Establishment is required to maintain the facility free of pests/insects. Ensure that third-party pest control is contacted to treat the cockroaches and that harborage conditions such as the soiled area between counters has been eliminated. A follow-up is issued for 12/14/2023 to ensure compliance. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

Operator states that employees are aware to never go from register/cash-handling to working with food without hand washing and will have a discussion with employees about increasing hand washing frequency when working with food.
